en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
The Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Chapter on Saṅghādisesa Offenses.
12. The Training Rule on Evil Conduct.
At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs who were pupils of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā were associating with [laypeople].
They lived with evil conduct, an evil reputation, and an evil public image; they harassed the community of bhikkhunīs and concealed each other’s faults.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:

“How can these bhikkhunīs live in such close association, with evil conduct, an evil reputation, and an evil public image, harassing the community of bhikkhunīs and concealing each other’s faults?”... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame, harassers of the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and concealers of each other’s faults?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...

“How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs live in association, behaving badly, having a bad reputation, being of evil repute, harassing the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and concealing one another’s offenses? This, monks,
will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence … And thus,
monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:”
“Now, if nuns live in association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame, causing vexation to the Saṅgha of nuns, and concealing one another’s faults,
those nuns should be addressed by the other nuns thus:
‘Sisters, you are living in association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame, causing vexation to the Saṅgha of nuns, and concealing one another’s faults.’”
"Live apart, sisters! The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the bhikkhunīs.

If those bhikkhunīs, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, those bhikkhunīs are to be formally admonished up to three times by the bhikkhunīs so that they may relinquish that course.
If, being admonished up to three times, they relinquish it, that is good.

If they do not desist, these bhikkhunīs too have committed an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which involves formal meeting of the Saṅgha and entails expulsion, after having been charged with it up to the third time.
"But those bhikkhunīs" refers to those who are fully ordained.
“They dwell in association” means:
they are said to dwell in association when they dwell in association through improper bodily and verbal conduct.
“Of evil conduct” means:
They are endowed with evil conduct.
They have a bad reputation means they have risen to prominence with an evil report.
"Of evil reputation" means they maintain their lives by means of an evil, wrong livelihood.
"Harassers of the community of bhikkhunīs" means...
They object when each other’s work is being performed.
They are concealers of each other’s offenses;
that is, they conceal each other’s offenses.
"Those nuns" refers to those nuns who are socializing.
"With nuns" refers to...
Other bhikkhunīs should [intervene]. Those who see or hear of it should say to them:
"Sisters, you are living in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, and of evil fame; you are harassers of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and concealers of each other's faults.
Separate yourselves, venerable ladies. The Saṅgha praises seclusion for sisters."
It should be said a second time;
it should be said a third time.
If they relinquish [the matter], that is good.
If they do not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Having heard [the charge], if they do not speak, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
Those nuns should be dragged even into the midst of the Saṅgha and addressed thus:
“Sisters, you are living in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, and of evil renown; you are harassers of the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs and concealers of each other’s faults.
Separate yourselves, noble ladies. The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters.
This should be said a second time as well.
A third time it should be said.
If they desist, that is good;
if they do not desist, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
Those bhikkhunīs should be admonished.
And thus, monks, should they be admonished:
A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the Saṅgha, noble ladies, hear me.

The bhikkhunīs named so-and-so and so-and-so live in association, behaving wickedly, having a wicked reputation, and being of wicked report; they cause harassment to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s offenses.
They do not relinquish that matter.”
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha formally admonish the nuns named so-and-so and so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.

The nuns named so-and-so and so-and-so live in close association, behaving wickedly, having a wicked reputation, and being of wicked report; they harass the community of nuns and conceal each other’s offenses.
They do not relinquish that course of action.
The Saṅgha formally admonishes the nuns named so-and-so and so-and-so for the purpose of relinquishing that matter.
Whichever noble lady approves of the formal admonition of the bhikkhunīs named so-and-so and so-and-so for the sake of relinquishing that matter, let her be silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
For a second time I speak this matter... [as before]...
For a third time I speak this matter: ...
[as before] ... The Saṅgha has formally admonished the bhikkhunīs named so-and-so and named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, I hold it thus.
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing;
for two proclamations, there are offenses of grave wrongdoing;
at the conclusion of the proclamation, there is an offense entailing suspension from the Saṅgha.
For those who have committed a *saṅghādisesa* offense, the *dukkaṭa* incurred by the motion (*ñatti*) and the *thullaccaya*s incurred by the two formal proclamations (*kammavācā*) are extinguished.
Two or three may be exhorted together; more than that should not be exhorted together.
These also [are] bhikkhunīs.
They are spoken of with reference to the preceding [offenses].
"Up to the third time" means that they incur [the offense] through being exhorted up to three times, not simultaneously with the transgression of the matter itself.
"Leading to expulsion" means one is expelled from the Saṅgha.
"Saṅghādisesa" [means...]
... [as before] ... for that reason also it is called a *saṅghādisesa*.
If they do not desist when there is a legitimate legal act (*dhammakamma*) while perceiving it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If they do not desist when there is a legitimate legal act while being in doubt about it, there is an offense of *saṅghādisesa*.
If, regarding an illegal act, they perceive it as an illegal act and do not relinquish it, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
If, regarding an illegal act, they perceive it as a legal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If, regarding an illegal act, they are uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and she perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense for those who do not formally admonish her.
For those who relinquish it,
for those who are insane,
and for those who are first offenders.
The training rule on the ninth Saṅghādisesa is finished.
